lines.en: I remember the moment I first read that novel.
The stifling hospital ward. The single PC in the lobby.
When I lined up to use the computer, a gentleman in a fedora gave up his seat for me. The monitor happened to be displaying my favorite novel platform.

I stared blankly at the screen, then entered some keywords. I think I entered about three, though I've forgotten what they were. But I remember the images that came to mind then: mechanical-pencil leads scattered across the classroom floor, and the indigo sky beyond the window.
All I know for certain is that, with the hand that had opened that window, I typed something and found that novel.
「Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World」
I survived because of that story.
「That it was never your fault this story came into being.」
Nausea churned in my stomach. Unable to bear the dizziness, I sank to the floor. I couldn't make out the text before my eyes.
「Han Sooyoung was tls123.」
I lay there for a long time, gasping. Only the same question circled in my head. Why. Why?
「For a thing like me」

I remained collapsed for a long time. I think I cried, too. But no amount of weeping or screaming could change sentences already written. Han Sooyoung had lived thirteen years for me, saved me with sentences carved out of herself. And then vanished.
「Kim Dok ja」
The [Fourth Wall] was calling me. I listened quietly to what it said next.
「You have to re ad」

I slowly got up. My reflection in the window was a mess. It hardly looked like an adult man's body anymore. I was shorter, my face younger. The coat I wore no longer suited me. After staring at my face for a long time, I took it off.
“······How many years has it been now?”
「Earth's ti me means no thing here.」
I knew what it meant.
This subway was where the ‘Oldest Dream’ dreamed. Time in other worldlines was no measure of the time passing here.
In fact, ever since coming to this subway, I had completely lost my sense of time.
“But there must still be some sense of how long it's been.”
「Rough ly 21,763 years.」
“Not as long as I thought. I'm still younger than the ‘Secretive Plotter,’ then.”
「Still a fledg ling」
I heard the [Fourth Wall] snickering. Without it, I would have gone mad here long ago.
With a soft crumbling sound, the tip of my little finger shrank.
When had it begun? My body was getting a little smaller even when I did nothing. Though, strictly speaking, I wasn't ‘doing nothing.’
“······Am I going to keep shrinking?”
I asked as I watched scraps of Story drift out the window.
“Where are all those Stories going?”
「The uni verse's uncon scious」
“Where's that?”
「World lines you're not aware of」
The task of the ‘Oldest Dream’ was to imagine every worldline. Even when my conscious mind was still, my unconscious constantly watched the worldlines.
「Those Sto ries will be born as other Kim Dok jas」
“As Kim Dokja?”
「Figu ratively speak ing」
Suddenly, I thought I understood what the [Fourth Wall] meant.
Stories flowing beyond galaxies toward other worldlines.
Those Stories were ‘me.’

Like the forty-nine percent of me who would be somewhere in the 1864th round with my companions, these fragments, too, might be born as ‘Kim Dokja’ somewhere in another worldline. After all, this universe moved in cycles like that.
“That's hardly enough to call ‘Kim Dokja.’ Fragments that small wouldn't resemble me.”
「Prob ably not」
Beings with names and faces different from mine. Even so, they would be born somewhere and imagine the universe. They would read stories and be moved by them, and watch over worldlines.
And in doing so, sustain this universe.
Somehow, I felt I understood a little of how this universe worked.
I held my crumbling finger to the window.
Then the process began to speed up, little by little.
「If you d o that」
“This is my atonement for this story.”
Stories began to scatter a little at a time, not only from my fingers, but from my shoulders and legs as well.
Those scattered Stories would fly through the universe and, somewhere in a worldline, become sentences that supported the universe.
「That although you grew up reading this story, you don't have to become it.」
Han Sooyoung, the author of ‘Ways of Survival’, had said that.
Her words had reached me clearly. Even so, I couldn't obey them.
After seeing a story like that, how could I choose anything else?
When I closed my eyes, an image of the whole universe took shape.
Han Sooyoung wrote the story.
Yoo Joonghyuk lived that story.
And I read that story.
That was how this world had just barely been completed.
「“Dokja-ssi.”」
Because this tragedy existed, some people had been able to meet.
Someone had been able to find salvation.
「Kim Dokja looked out at the endless universe.」
I knew my future now. Every time I read something, I would break apart. My broken Stories would scatter through countless worldlines, becoming ‘gazes’ that sustained this universe.
I would lose my memories and the things I loved. In the end, all that would remain was the desire to see the ‘next story.’
Without that desire, this universe couldn't continue.
A universe whose story continued only if someone watched.
In this universe, standing still meant death.
Tsu-chuchuchuchu······.
Countless particles of ‘me’ spread into countless worldlines. My Stories were scattering faster and faster.
“Once I forget everything······it won't hurt anymore, will it?”
「Be cause you won't re member」
For someone in whom even the traces of loss had vanished, there was no loss.
I picked up the smartphone from the floor and spoke.
“······Will I have time to read it once more?”
I opened the ‘Ways of Survival’ file and scrolled down past the [Author's Words] I had barely managed to read.
「Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World」.
I began reading the novel from the beginning.
I read Yoo Joonghyuk's third round. Some stories were familiar; others felt new to me now.
The final version was exactly the same as the original I knew.
There was no ‘Kim Dokja’ in it.
Ssssh······.
As my Stories scattered, sentences from ‘Ways of Survival’ filled me again in equal measure. When I was tired, I closed my eyes and rested a while. After resting, I started reading again.
The fifth round, the sixth······the sixty-fourth······the 129th······.
The 672nd round.
The 914th round.
The 1642nd round······.
The pages scrolled down, and I felt joy or sorrow a few times.

I wished I could leave comments. I wanted to tell Han Sooyoung how I felt once more. That I had made it this far because of the story you gave me. That I loved your story more than anyone in the world.
And so I read, and read, and read.
How long had I been reading that story?
Tsu-chuchuchuchu······.
When I finally reached the epilogue, my sight suddenly blurred.
I wondered whether I had gone blind from reading the novel so much.
[The update is complete.]
My vision slowly returned. What I saw weren't proper sentences. The sentences and paragraphs had all been fragmented.
Writing that didn't take the shape of a complete novel.
Yet, for some reason, I could read it.
「One world had fallen to ruin, and a new world was being born.」
My heart pounded.
There was a story I knew very well.
「I was the only reader who knew how this world would end.」
I was in that story.
「“I am Yoo Joonghyuk.”」
「“Ah, now that you mention it, I haven't introduced myself. My name is Han Sooyoung. I serve as Cha Sangkyung-nim's aide in the group.”」
And so were they.
「“If the ‘scenarios’ hadn't started, what would have happened to us?”」
「“Dokja-ssi, your constellation sponsor wouldn't happen to be something like the ‘One-Eyed Fortune Teller,’ would it?”」
「“Dokja-ssi, have you ever thrown a grenade?”」
「“Ajusshi, is there something you like to eat?”」
I made my way through the scenarios with them.
「Hyung, are you a god?」
「“Load.”」
「“Everyone, fight without worrying. I won't let anyone die.”」
「“You bastards! Leaving me out again······!”」
「“The one I like isn't you, it's the Demon King of Salvation―”」
「[Baat!]」
I lived my life with them.
「“The next scenario is······.”」
I faced trials, and found myself on the brink of death again and again.
I met constellations.
I overcame impossible scenarios time after time.
And finally, I reached the end of those hellish scenarios.
「[Your ■■ is ‘Eternity.’]」
My companions returned to everyday life.

「People were rebuilding a collapsed internet café. People sticking torn game posters back up. In a world that had overcome the apocalypse, people sought entertainment again. Watching them, Yoo Joonghyuk quietly clenched his right hand, which hadn't held a mouse in so long.」
「Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung enrolled in a temporary school. Neither elementary, middle, nor high school, but literally a ‘temporary school.’ Shin Yoosung was amazed that such a place could exist.」

「After staring for a long time at the ruins of ‘Taepung Girls' High School’, Lee Jihye walked onto the school field. The very field where she had once run around with her friends. She quietly studied its worn lines, then carefully took up a starting stance.」
Reading the stories of what my companions did next, I wiped my eyes again and again.
This was the ending of this story.
They were living there, without a doubt. Eating, sleeping, meeting one another and talking. I was there, too.
Forty-nine percent of me. A Kim Dokja who remembered his companions, but didn't know ‘Ways of Survival’·····.
「And Kim Dokja read that sentence.」
But.
「“Who the hell are you?”」
What on earth was this?
「“Tell me. Who are you?”」
This couldn't happen.
「“There's no doubt. Kim Dokja is still there.”」
Why.
「“If I run once more, do you think I will see it better?”」
Tsu-chuchuchuchuchu······.
The story continued. The story that should have ended didn't end.
More precisely, they chose ‘not to end it.’
「[The stigma ‘Group Regression Lv.1’ activates!]」
I read that sentence in something close to a scream.
This was something that should never happen. It was a sentence that must never, ever be written.
Indifferently, the sentence led into the next.
「“Remember. We only get one chance.”」
My companions were fighting again.
That hell of scenarios was a place they should never return to, whatever the reason. Yet they returned.
「“Kid, aren't you tossing a coin this time?”
“It'll be the same whether I do or not.”
“Why?”
“Even if it came up once in a hundred tosses, even if only one percent of hyung remained there. We'd still have to go save him. That one percent is hyung, too.”」
And the scenarios began. Amid a spectacle of coins bursting through the air, the dokkaebis of the 〈Star Stream〉 looked on in shock.
With the constellations' interest at fever pitch, my companions shouted.
「“Hey, Abaddon! Choose me! I'm definitely going to be a hundred times stronger than that black-clad bastard!”」
「“Admiral! Are you there? You're watching me, right!”」
「“I don't need a constellation sponsor, so just give me coins.”」
「“······Black Flame Dragon, stop messaging me while I'm still asking nicely. I said I wasn't choosing you this time.”」
They were insane.
「“Hehe, it certainly took you long enough to get to Chungmuro. Can you even save that weakling at this rate? For your information, this whole area is already my territory······.”
“Shut up and hand over the flag, Gong Pildu.”」
Insane people were clearing the scenarios in insane ways.
Crises struck again and again, but my companions wouldn't yield.
「[Incarnation ‘Lee Jihye’ activates the stigma ‘Transmission Lv.1’!」
「“You black-clad bastard! No wonder you were the only one who got stronger, using something like this!”」
[Transmission]. A regressor-exclusive skill that let them relearn skills by vividly recalling memories of a previous life.
「“Uriel! Great Sage, Heaven's Equal! Abyssal Black Flame Dragon!”」
With help from the constellations as well, my companions cleared the scenarios without a hitch. Their pace was truly terrifying.
「“We can clear this one with avatars. No one needs to die.”」
But they didn't always have everything their way.
「“Supreme King. Sorry, but you'll have to die here.”」
There were traitors among those who had regressed with them.
「“If you regained your original strength, even the three of us together wouldn't stand a chance.”
“But right now, it's a different story.”」
I bit my lip.
People who had joined the regression with ulterior motives from the start.
They had deliberately chosen the early scenarios, when Yoo Joonghyuk was with Yoo Mia. They must have decided that was when he was weakest.
「But they had miscalculated.」
As Yoo Joonghyuk spoke, a long sword was drawn from Yoo Mia's mouth.
「Black Heavenly Demon Sword.」

A top-class item only obtainable in the middle scenarios was in Yoo Joonghyuk's hand. Goosebumps rose on my skin. Who would have thought he could use Yoo Mia's ‘Inventory’ like that······? Radiating terrifying bloodlust, Yoo Joonghyuk declared:
「“Farewell.”」
Scattered sentences continued after that.
「“I'm this round's ‘Demon King of Salvation’!”
“No, we agreed it would be me! That modifier's mine, noona!”」
None of my companions would give way.
「Many constellations express hostility toward the incarnations of ‘Kim Dokja’s Company’!」
They compromised with no one.
Without Kim Dokja, ‘Kim Dokja’s Company’ cleared the scenarios neither too quickly nor too slowly.
Some scenes were described, while others were omitted. The farther I read, the more disjointed they became. It was as if sketches of ideas had simply been left as they were.
My companions would be in Scenario 20, then in Scenario 15, then in Scenario 35. But they were certainly there. I could imagine them.
「They ran across the blank space.」
My companions racing across the snowfield of the scenarios. One sentence, then another, they advanced. They were getting closer to me.
Watching them, I cried and fell asleep, again and again. The fainter my consciousness grew, the clearer my desire became. I knew I shouldn't think it, but couldn't stop.
「I want to read a little more of this story.」
I read one broken sentence, then the next. Haltingly, I imagined what lay between them.
The point the author couldn't control, and the reader couldn't predict.
In those spaces between the lines, where nothing was expressed in sentences, my companions completed the scenarios little by little.
「Between the lines, where no one could intrude on their lives, they were the gods (神) of this story.」

Reading that story, I lost consciousness several times. I read more and more slowly, and my Stories gradually disappeared. My companions' sentences steadily accumulated. Through Scenario 98, then Scenario 99. The sentences they wrote with their lives piled up, exactly one at a time. And finally.
「They had finally reached the ending she had written.」
The final sentence arrived. That was the end of ‘Ways of Survival’. A story that seemed to have been left unfinished. A story that had never reached a proper conclusion.
Beyond its final sentence, I heard a sound. Like someone calling out. Or knocking on a door.
My smartphone clicked off, and its black screen reflected my face, now a child's. I was crying.
「Kim Dokja slowly raised his head.」
The subway's faint vibrations. When had they begun?
Bang―!
Someone was knocking on the rear door of the carriage.
“Run! Just a little farther!”
Han Sooyoung broke through the waves of constellations with her companions.
Fragments of the shattering Ark, and the [Final Wall] revealed in the distance.
A Giant Story's blessing enveloped the companions as though to protect them.
[The Giant Story ‘Adversaries of Fate’ begins its story.]
A new Giant Story they had obtained in this round.
Without it, they would have died many times over.
In the distance, constellations were advancing on them. Myth-grade constellations of 〈Vedas〉 and 〈Papyrus〉 charged like enraged beasts.
「Unlike the previous round, there are no ‘Outer Gods’ to help them this time.」
An overwhelming disadvantage in military strength. Yet they held their ground because the strongest group of regressors in history was supporting them.
The incarnations of China and India took the front.

At a signal from China's Fei Hu, the incarnations of his faction, [A-Q], drew their weapons in unison. India's Ranveer Khan joined them as though unwilling to be outdone. As the incarnations of [Tramurti] following him drew their spears, a sandstorm began blowing through the area.
[Justice], led by Selena Kim, and [Solzhenitsyn], commanded by Iris, who had come with them, took the two flanks.
But the tide of battle was still against them.
[Go. I'll handle things here.]
[If you fail to bring my disciple back, I'll have your lives.]
Kyrgios and the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint. They, too, were among the hundred regressors. As their weapons swept the battlefield, transcendents from Murim rushed to support them.
Kwoooooom!

Made even stronger by regression, Kyrgios's punches and the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's sword strikes shook the battlefield as though competing. Constellations screamed as they were torn apart in the silver storm.
They had to open the [Wall] while the others bought whatever time they could.
「It is a wall they have already opened once.」
Looking up at the barrier they had finally reached, Han Sooyoung spoke.
“Jang Hayoung.”
“Yep.”
As though she'd been waiting, Jang Hayoung reached out.
Back in the scenarios once more, she was now a full-fledged ‘King of Transcendents.’
[The ‘Wall of Impossible Communication’ has regained its place.]
As though responding to their Giant Story, the [Final Wall] began to tremble.
“Yoo Sangah.”
Yoo Sangah nodded and stepped forward.
[The ‘Wall that Decides Samsara’ has regained its place.]
「[You······I see······after all those long years, you have come full circle, back here again, my arhat.]」

Sakyamuni's Story, murmured in a low voice. The Sakyamuni of this worldline accepted Yoo Sangah's existence without much difficulty. Having gone through long cycles of reincarnation himself, he understood the laws of this universe.
“Jung Heewon, Lee Gilyoung.”
The [Wall that Divides Good and Evil], received from ‘Metatron’ and ‘Agares.’
Jung Heewon was first to put her hand against the [Final Wall].
「[······Have you truly seen what lies beyond the Wall?]」

This worldline's Metatron was astonished by the companions' existence. He accepted 〈Eden〉's destruction and acknowledged it as an outcome that couldn't be changed. Then he made a slightly different choice from the previous round. The archangels of 〈Eden〉 helping the incarnations were proof of that. But Metatron wasn't the only one to make an unusual choice.
「[How interesting. You dare ask me, a demon king, for the [Wall].]」

The demon kings and angels who had fought to tear one another apart in the Great War of Saints and Demons were on their side this time. They had each made that choice only for their own survival, but it was still a tremendous help to 〈Kim Dokja’s Company〉.
[The ‘Wall that Divides Good and Evil’ has regained its place.]
[Many constellations unleash their Status toward 〈Kim Dokja’s Company〉!]
Not all constellations had become allies. The vast majority of the 〈Star Stream〉 were still enemies, and only a few constellations helped them.
Even so, the companions had made it this far safely. Deep scars marked their bodies, but they hadn't lost anyone.
They had managed it because no one had been greedy, and everyone shared the same goal.
Lastly, Han Sooyoung looked back at Lee Hyunsung.
A pale-faced Kim Dokja was on his back. More precisely, the avatar Kim Dokja had left behind.
Looking at him, Han Sooyoung said:
“Help us, Kim Dokja.”
He, too, was certainly Kim Dokja.
Just as the Han Sooyoung of the 1863rd round had certainly been ‘Han Sooyoung.’
“The other me might not want this. That story······ended there······.”
Kim Dokja, speaking haltingly. He had now accepted that he was the avatar of ‘Kim Dokja’. Han Sooyoung watched him quietly, then spoke.
“Let's meet the other you and ask him.”
Kim Dokja smiled sadly. He looked at Han Sooyoung, then at each of the companions' faces.
“If this is the story you want······.”
A pale hand touched the [Final Wall].
The Final Wall's last fragment was the [Fourth Wall].
And he, Kim Dokja's avatar, shared part of that key.
Tsu-chuchuchuchu······!
Kim Dokja's body trembled unsteadily, as though this world refused to acknowledge his existence.
Then, with a cracking sound, part of the Wall opened. Kim Dokja shook as though electrocuted, then fainted. Lee Hyunsung took him on his back.
Flicking his Black Heavenly Demon Sword clean, Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“Full speed.”
At the signal, the companions began to run.
“Keep going, everyone! We're almost there!”
“I still have Life and Death Pills, so tell me right away if you're hurt at all!”

The voices of the companions encouraging one another. Listening to them, Han Sooyoung ran, too. A pure white snowfield spread before her. Letters lay piled like snow all across it. Han Sooyoung stepped on the letters and leaped.
Had her 1863rd-round self written this story in the revised version?
Had she thought of Kim Dokja's story, of the epilogue that followed?
······She didn't know.
That, she simply couldn't remember.
Just then, something settled on Han Sooyoung's eyelashes.
She rubbed her eyes without thinking, and something like snow came away on her hand.
「······That bastard—she told me she'd been a poor, bookish girl.」
White letters fluttered through the air like snow. Sentences that were certainly there, but couldn't be seen because they were so close to pure white.
「Han Sooyoung.」
Han Sooyoung stared blankly at the sentence that had fallen onto her hand.
「Your story······.」

These were Kim Dokja's sentences. They were impressions written by none other than Kim Dokja himself. Han Sooyoung clenched them tightly. Like starlight driven away by dawn, the sentences crumbled in her hand.
「Don't worry. I'll read it. Even if it's over three thousand chapters.」
They were the sentences she had wanted so badly, yet they weren't hers.
Memories came flooding in. Emotions another self had felt.
Han Sooyoung could still feel them vividly. Resentment with nowhere to go spread through her heart.
「Kim Dokja is beyond this snowfield.」
The Kim Dokja who made Kim Dokja who he was. The Kim Dokja who remembered ‘Ways of Survival’. The Kim Dokja who chose memories of her book over his happy memories······.
“Damn it······damn it!”
A book written by someone who was her, yet wasn't. That book had saved Kim Dokja, and ruined him. And now she had to take responsibility for the ending of this tragedy another self had made.
Just then, a faint light appeared in the distance.
Rrrrrumble······.
Something was racing beyond the distant snowfield. The companions looked at one another at once. Everyone knew what it was.
「It was a subway train.」
“Chimera Dragon!”
Summoned with a roar, the Chimera Dragon took them on its back and flew. Accelerating in an instant, it cut through the sky toward the rear of the train. Almost there. Just a little farther―
[Gyaaaaaah!]
Suddenly, the Chimera Dragon screamed and lost its balance. Startled, Shin Yoosung looked back. Something was biting its tail.
【Grrrrrrrr······!】

Huge wild dogs resembling black shadows were tearing at the dragon's tail and wings. Wild dogs that had come through a portal in the sky. Chunks of the Chimera Dragon's flesh scattered across the white snowfield.
“Hounds Pursuing the Abyss?”

They had seen them before. Hounds from another dimension that had attacked the ‘Secretive Plotter’ and the people of the 999th round. Terrifying monsters said to attack worldline wanderers who violated probability.
But why were those hounds attacking them?
Yoo Joonghyuk spoke with a low groan.
“······Apparently, they judged ‘Group Regression’ a threat to the worldlines.”
“Goddamn it······.”
The number of hounds coming through the portal was increasing exponentially.
There were larger hounds, too. A powerful presence unlike any they had seen before. Roaring across the snowfield, the hounds launched themselves through the air all at once.
Just as the black mass of hounds fell upon the companions.
A rumble rang out, as though the sky were collapsing.
Golden lightning surged, sending the hounds flying. Yoo Sangah was first to recognize who it was.
“Great Sage, Heaven's Equal!”
A golden band shining proudly. The master of the Ruyi Jingu Bang was grinning.
[Leave this to me.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ unleashes his Status!]
He wasn't the only one.
Others had followed them through the passage they opened in the [Final Wall].
[A chance to show what happens when I use both hands!]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ releases all his seals!]
Then a noble archangel's flames burned the hounds.
[I'm not as strong as my 999th-round self······but buying time is no problem.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ raises the flames of hell!]
The flames of [Hell Flames Ignition], blazing gloriously between pure white wings. With a faint smile, Uriel spoke.
[Take care of Kim Dokja, Heewon.]
Using the opening the constellations made, the Chimera Dragon finally bit the rear of the train. But even its fangs couldn't break the train's hard exterior.
“Master! Together!”
Holding a sword in each hand, Lee Jihye flew up from the dragon's back.
The Maritime War God's [Twin Dragon Sword] and Goryeo’s First Sword's [Peerless Sword]. The two blades were in her hands.
[The constellation ‘Goryeo’s First Sword’ bestows his blessing!]
[The constellation ‘Maritime War God’ cheers on his incarnation!]
Fourth Form (四式).
Fourth Sword that Beheads the Emptiness (四劍斬虛).

The very technique Cheok Jungyeong had once used against ‘The Indescribable Distance.’ Lee Jihye could now use that sword strike, too, though she had yet to master it. It was a miracle made possible by her grueling training on ‘Reincarnation Island’ and her astonishing talent.
Kwakwakwakwa!
The subway's exterior, untouched by the dragon's fangs, gradually crumpled under her repeated sword strikes. Seizing that opening, Yoo Joonghyuk moved his [Black Heavenly Demon Sword].
Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship (破天劍道).
Secret Art (秘傳奧義).
Meteor Slash (流星斬).
The destructive arc of the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] struck the rear of the train.
When the thick dust cleared, there was a small hole in its rear.
“We did it! Everyone, inside!”
The companions swiftly entered the train.
All except exactly two people.
“Yoo Joonghyuk! Behind you!”
【Grrrrrr!】

Hounds the constellations hadn't managed to stop were surging toward the rear. Yoo Joonghyuk met them head-on, unleashing the full power of Transcendent Form. Beating back the hounds with a storm of sword strikes, he shouted.
“Go ahead! I'll follow shortly!”
Han Sooyoung bit her lip.
This was Yoo Joonghyuk, the strongest of them all. He could now contend even with Myth-grade constellations. The abyss hounds wouldn't defeat him easily.
“······Don't die.”
Leaving those words behind, Han Sooyoung went straight into the train. The interior looked exactly like that of the Line 3 train they remembered.
「The very subway where they had left Kim Dokja.」
Han Sooyoung quickly checked the carriage information. With a crackle, the carriage number appeared. She shouted reflexively.
“Kim Dokja is in carriage 3807! Everyone, head to the front!”
It was like the time they had obtained the Giant Story ‘Demon Realm's Spring.’ The companions seemed to realize it, too.
“It's like when we fought Surya. I'll open the front door!”
Lee Hyunsung rushed forward, swelling every muscle in his body as he cried out.
“Haaaaaah!”
As [Great Mountain Push], which had surpassed its proficiency limit, activated, the thick subway door creaked open.
[The Giant Story ‘Demon Realm's Spring’ begins its story!]
[‘Stage Transformation’ activates!]
A Giant Story they had achieved because everyone had their role. Its blessing was helping them now.
When Lee Hyunsung couldn't open a door, Yoo Sangah found its button. When even Yoo Sangah couldn't open one, Lee Gilyoung opened it by sending insects to wear down its parts.
Opening, and opening, and opening again. As more doors opened, their faces flushed with excitement.
「Kim Dokja is definitely on the other side.」
Everyone felt it. A black door. This was surely the [Final Door].
“······Urgh, even my stigma isn't enough.”
But the door refused to open.
“I can't find a button, either.”
“The insects say they can't work out its structure.”
“Should I try breaking it with a skill?”
Even Lee Jihye's sword strikes and Lee Hyunsung's [Great Mountain Smash] couldn't budge the door. The companions looked at one another. Why wouldn't this one door open?
Then Yoo Sangah spoke.
“Wait. This door is the same as the one Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi broke back then.”
“Yoo Joonghyuk did?”
“Yes. In the third round, Joonghyuk-ssi broke through this door―”
Han Sooyoung instinctively looked back. Yoo Joonghyuk hadn't come with them. He would be fighting the ‘Hounds Pursuing the Abyss’ at the rear of the train.
Then Shin Yoosung shouted.
“The hounds are coming!”
Before they knew it, hounds were creeping through the opening they had made.
Panic rose in her. What had happened to Yoo Joonghyuk? Surely they hadn't―
“Hold the rear!”
“Unnie! Hurry!”

There was no time to think. Lee Hyunsung rushed forward like a tank, withstanding the hounds' fangs through [Steel Transformation], while Lee Jihye and Jung Heewon drew their swords and beat them back.

“Are you any different?”

[The Story ‘One Who Opposes the Extraordinary’ grieves.]

Words she hadn't managed to let go of. She had endured life by writing them somewhere. Don't regress. Live in the present. Repeating those trite words from the past, she had endured each moment. For two years.
“You haven't been able to forget anything, either.”
“Shut up.”
Leaping up in an instant, Han Sooyoung punched Yoo Joonghyuk in the face. Every time their fists met, the Stories they shared and had built together shook.
[The Story ‘King of Kaizenix’ wavers.]
She'd believed she'd worked hard to hold on. She'd thought a great deal of time had passed, measured by the sentences she'd written. Breathing, eating, sleeping. Han Sooyoung had survived like that.
「You don't have to regress to be a regressor.」
But could she say she had been living?
「Some people spend their entire lives in a past that has already gone.」
As the bones in their fists shattered, Stories scattered a little at a time. Raw memories preserved without a single revision. Unconsciously, Han Sooyoung gathered the scattering Stories.
Because she didn't want to lose even one. Because she didn't want to forget even one.
「For the past two years, she hadn't moved a single step.」
Gasping, Han Sooyoung spoke.
“What would doing this now change?”

“I gathered so many Stories, but I still don't know what my ■■ is.”
Fierce Stories burst in the air. Paying no heed to the damage to his precious Stories, Yoo Joonghyuk swung his fist.
“You wrote my story. Then you must know where my story should end.”
For an instant, sentences flowed through Han Sooyoung's mind.
「Had Yoo Joonghyuk really come here to obtain the [Final Ark]?」
A belated realization swept over her.
The regressor exhausted by scenarios had, in truth, been able to live because the scenarios existed.
Yoo Joonghyuk gathered all his Stories. The Stories of Yoo Joonghyuk, who had finally escaped the curse of regression, now bared their hostility toward Han Sooyoung.
“Give it everything, Han Sooyoung.”
「This was Yoo Joonghyuk's last fight.」
Every cell in her body rang an alarm.
A regressor who had repeated his long life.
An emotion rose in the eyes she had described dozens, hundreds of times. Han Sooyoung knew what it was.
Yoo Joonghyuk wanted to die here.
At the hands of none other than the one who had written his first sentence.
“Fuck! You've never done what I wanted, not even once!”
Kwoooooom!

A roar erupted as though a star had exploded.

Her whole body hurt as if it had been beaten. Every bone in her outstretched right fist shattered. Her companions' shouts and people's screams. Amid the pain tearing through her ears, Han Sooyoung endured the impact. Her body was in tatters.
Yoo Joonghyuk lay collapsed before her.
Her heart pounded.
“Yoo Joonghyuk?”

“······A little different from the Dark Castle, huh?”

“Doesn't seem that different.”
“You son of a bitch······.”
They fell face down side by side onto the ground. Han Sooyoung crawled toward him. She didn't think she could calm down without hitting him once more, somehow.

“······They said Kim Dokja scattered into the universe.”
Kim Dokja's soul, scattered into tiny pieces. How much Kim Dokja was in those little fragments? Han Sooyoung didn't know, either.

“Do you think he's found happiness?”
The moment she heard that, Han Sooyoung felt as though something had ended.

An awful pain seized her heart. She distinctly heard a sound like something breaking. The sound of one story ending. The sound of their long mourning finally ending. The sound of someone who had lived only in the past finally letting that past go. At that moment, Han Sooyoung was gripped by a strange sense of guilt.
“Kim Dokja······.”
「Hadn't she actually hoped he wouldn't give up?」
Even if everyone else let go of this long grief, hadn't she hoped at least one person would keep doing those damned things, ruining his own life in the process?

“I'm sure he's doing well. He's strong.”
“He'll be making a life for himself and living happily there, too. Maybe reading another strange book.”
“Even if we found him, he wouldn't remember anything.”
Their mourning ended there.

“We don't know that. If Ways of Survival exists where he was born.”
For a moment, she didn't know why she'd said it.
“I mean, Ways of Survival······.”
As though defying her will, her mouth murmured.
「Kim Dokja, who became the ‘Oldest Dream,’ scattered throughout the universe.」
Her mind spilled out confused sentences.
「This universe is sustained by the imagination of that ‘Oldest Dream.’」

「“Ajusshi in another worldline would like books, too, right?”」

Kim Dokja, far away on the other side of the universe, reading someone's novel with an expression unfamiliar to her.

A way to bring Kim Dokja back without ruining the lives of the Kim Dokjas reincarnated in other worldlines.

“If the story he dreams······is the same story we want······?”
A black shadow falling over her head broke her reverie.
“We were going to build a park here, but you two have made a complete mess of it.”
How long had Anna Croft been standing there?
“Are you thinking of crossing worldlines again?”

It was nonsense to begin with. Making Kim Dokjas in other worldlines dream of the novel she'd written? Nothing could be more ridiculous.
Above all, there was no longer any way to cross worldlines from this world.
But Anna Croft's expression was a little strange.
“I thought a day like this might come.”
Anna Croft's eyes shone red. Her gaze was on the museum spire.
The model of the [Final Ark].
Her heart beat slowly. It couldn't be possible. It couldn't, and yet······why?
Rrrrrumble.

An Ark. It was very small, but it was unmistakably an Ark.

The slowly rising Ark opened like a capsule, revealing its interior. A tiny [Final Ark] that looked barely large enough for one person.
“It can be used. But only one person can board it.”
